name: Assyrian Neo-Aramaic

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Assyrian Neo-Aramaic (assy1241).

notes:
Assyrian Neo-Aramaic (Suret), a modern Semitic (Afroasiatic, Northeastern Neo-Aramaic) language written in the East Syriac abjad. The spec describes UNPOINTED East Syriac spelling: vowel quality is written by the East Syriac vowel points and consonant quality by the qushshaya and rukkakha dots and by majliana, and none of those marks are part of the letter string this spec receives. What the bare letters still decide is the matres lectionis and the word-edge behaviour of the letters that carry them.

Matres lectionis. Alaph, waw and yudh double as vowel letters. Alaph is the glottal stop word-initially, where it carries an initial vowel; word-finally it is the vowel of the determined-state ending -a, and medially it is ambiguous between the glottal stop and a written long vowel, so both readings stand in the lattice with the consonant first. Waw is consonantal /w/ word-initially and otherwise writes the back rounded vowels /u uː o oː/; yudh is consonantal /j/ word-initially and otherwise writes /i iː e eː/. The ordering inside each list is a frequency claim measured on the shipped WikiPron gold, not an editorial guess: word-final alaph is a vowel in 3232 of 3236 gold sites and [ɑː] in 2314 of them; word-initial alaph is [ʔ] in 363 of 382; word-initial waw is [w] in 21 of 24 and word-initial yudh is [j] in 120 of 135.

Begadkepat. Historic postvocalic spirantization of the six plosives is fossilized rather than synchronic here, and unpointed spelling does not say which reflex a given token has, so both reflexes stand in the lattice. Word position does discriminate: word-finally the fricative reflex leads for beth, gamal, dalath, kaph and taw, while pe does not spirantize at all, because *p is merged into /p/ outside the Tyari, Barwari and Chaldean varieties and [f] survives mainly in loanwords. Medially the plosive leads for all six, so the letters keep their plain values there and no medial spirantization is declared.

Heth is [x] rather than [ħ] in Assyrian Neo-Aramaic, so the velar fricative leads and the pharyngeal is kept as a minority reading. Ayin is retained as /ʕ/. The affricates /t͡ʃ d͡ʒ ʒ/ are written with the majliana mark on kaph, gamal, zain and shin; since the mark is absent from unpointed text they are carried as minority readings of those letters. Gemination, stress and the emphatic spread of the emphatic consonants are not encoded.

Doubled waw. A written ⟨ܘܘ⟩ digraph is not a doubled vowel letter. The shipped gold has 27 rows containing ⟨ܘܘ⟩, reducing to 18 unique headwords: 16 carry it non-initially (13 word-medially, 3 word-finally) and 2 open with it. Across the 16 non-initial headwords no gold reading repeats [uː], so the digraph is given its own entry, [uw] ahead of [uww], instead of resolving to the two single-waw vowel readings. That is a distributional finding measured on the shipped gold, not a claim drawn from a grammar; no citation for the convention itself is offered. The second waw is not invariably consonantal: ⟨ܓܝܘܘ⟩ reads [ɡiːwoː], with the FIRST waw consonantal and the SECOND the vowel [oː]. That headword is also the only place in the class where the digraph entry costs anything, PER 0.3333 with the two single-waw readings against 0.5000 with the digraph. It pays for itself elsewhere: ⟨ܗܘܘ⟩ falls from 1.2500 to 0.7500 and ⟨ܡܥܘܘܟܐ⟩ from 0.5556 to 0.3333. The digraph reading is confined to non-initial position. Word-initial waw is consonantal /w/, as the matres lectionis paragraph above states, so a digraph entry in the general table would outrank that rule and make the engine open a word with a vowel the spec says cannot stand there, giving [uw] for ⟨ܘܘ⟩ and [uwɑː] for ⟨ܘܘܐ⟩. The entry is therefore keyed word_initial in positional_graphemes, the same shape the single letters ⟨ܐ⟩, ⟨ܘ⟩ and ⟨ܝ⟩ already use. Word-initially ⟨ܘܘ⟩ therefore reads [wuː] or [woː], the initial consonant followed by the vowel the second waw carries, which is what the two single letters would give. The two gold entries there, [waw] and [wawwa], score the same either way (0.6667 and 0.8000), so the correction costs no PER; it removes an output the spec's own phonology forbids.

sources.notes: Consulted for the pointing system: the qushshaya (dot above, hard) and rukkakha (dot below, soft) dots on the six begadkepat letters, and the majliana mark that turns gamal into [d͡ʒ], kaph into [t͡ʃ], and zain or shin into [ʒ] in the Madnhaya (East Syriac) variant.
